html:
DAT (Chen et al., ICCV 2023): a x4 upscaler for clean (bicubic) images that alternates spatial and channel attention, in three sizes (DAT, DAT-2, DAT-light). Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

Details
  • Paper: Dual Aggregation Transformer for Image Super-Resolution, ICCV 2023, 2023-08-07
  • Original code: https://github.com/zhengchen1999/DAT at 1645c64fad7c
  • Code licence: Apache-2.0 (permissive); files: LICENSE
  • Weights licence: Apache-2.0
  • Licence evidence: https://github.com/zhengchen1999/DAT/blob/1645c64fad7c94d94abd090bd1319eec1f26f7cc/LICENSE ; https://github.com/zhengchen1999/DAT/blob/1645c64fad7c94d94abd090bd1319eec1f26f7cc/README.md (pretrained models: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1iBdf_-LVZuz_PAbFtuxSKd_11RL1YKxM)
  • Training data: DIV2K (NTIRE 2017 super-resolution, 1000 2K images), Flickr2K (2650 2K Flickr images, EDSR) (options/Train/train_DAT_x4.yml: DF2K (DIV2K + Flickr2K), bicubic-downsampled, fine-tuned from the x2 model.)
    • dat-2-x4: DIV2K (NTIRE 2017 super-resolution, 1000 2K images), Flickr2K (2650 2K Flickr images, EDSR) (options/Train/train_DAT_2_x4.yml: DF2K (DIV2K + Flickr2K), bicubic-downsampled, fine-tuned from the x2 model.)
    • dat-light-x4: DIV2K (NTIRE 2017 super-resolution, 1000 2K images), Flickr2K (2650 2K Flickr images, EDSR) (options/Train/train_DAT_light_x4.yml: DF2K (DIV2K + Flickr2K), bicubic-downsampled, fine-tuned from the x2 model.)
  • Kernel libraries: cudnn_hacc
  • Variants: dat-x4, dat-2-x4, dat-light-x4
  • Outputs: image
  • Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): dat-x4 1024x1024 (10.1 GiB peak allocated, 14.9 reserved); dat-2-x4 1024x1024 (10.1 GiB peak allocated, 14.1 reserved); dat-light-x4 1024x1024 (6.3 GiB peak allocated, 7.4 reserved)
  • dat-x4 512x512, first call: portable + torch.compile 43 s (cold Inductor cache).
  • dat-2-x4 512x512, first call: portable + torch.compile 44 s (cold Inductor cache).
  • dat-light-x4 512x512, first call: portable + torch.compile 37 s (cold Inductor cache).
  • dat-x4 original 512x512: .half() on 1 modules, fp16 inputs; upstream dat_model.py test, float32, no chop
  • dat-2-x4 original 512x512: .half() on 1 modules, fp16 inputs; upstream dat_model.py test, float32, no chop
  • dat-light-x4 original 512x512: .half() on 1 modules, fp16 inputs; upstream dat_model.py test, float32, no chop
  • dat-x4 load / first call: original 2.2 s / 6.13 s, portable 0.89 s / 2.36 s, kernels 2.55 s / 2.467 s
  • dat-2-x4 load / first call: original 2.04 s / 5.516 s, portable 14.55 s / 2.72 s, kernels 1.61 s / 2.031 s
  • dat-light-x4 load / first call: original 3.48 s / 2.721 s, portable 0.21 s / 1.304 s, kernels 1.25 s / 1.152 s
  • Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

Measured

DIV2K validation HR images and the official bicubic LR images (x4 or x2, the model's scale), one pass without tiles; PSNR and SSIM (Gaussian 11 x 11, sigma 1.5) on the Y channel (BT.601) of the output rounded to uint8, scale px border cropped, averaged over the images. Real-ESRGAN is trained for real-world degradations, not bicubic, so its PSNR is low: the numbers compare our modes with the original, not with PSNR-oriented upscalers. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 3.6e-06 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.0012 and p99 <= 0.0044 (absolute error of the output image).
